title:
Super-Cross-Reactive
Recognition Enables Preclinical
Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease
content:
Abstract
Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is impeded by the subtle, heterogeneous nature of fluid biomarkers during the disease’s initial phases. Current detection tools, which target single biomarkers, often lack the necessary sensitivity and specificity for presymptomatic screening. To address this, we develop a machine learning-informed supramolecular sensor array that leverages a holistic design to overcome the limitations of “lock-and-key” recognition. By engineering macrocyclic receptors with semiselective properties, we generate a competitive signal transduction process characterized by multiple equilibria and nonlinear responses. This design confers high-dimensional cross-reactivity, delineating distinct fluorescent fingerprints for specific AD stages. The array achieves 100% diagnostic accuracy in cerebrospinal fluid from 1-month-old rat models─predating conventional ELISA detection by 3 months and behavioral symptoms by 4 months. Crucially, the array identifies human patients at the subjective cognitive decline stage with >95% accuracy. This work presents a clinically viable tool for early AD diagnosis and establishes a generalizable, modular framework for multiplexed biomarker analysis in neurodegenerative diseases.

title:
Construction of Divergent
Enantioenriched 3D-Fluoro
Scaffolds via Ni(0) π-Lewis Base-Mediated Umpolung of
Fluorodienes
content:
Abstract
Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies. Herein, we report an umpolung strategy that utilizes low-valent Ni(0) as a π-Lewis base activator for gem-difluorodienes and leverages d → π* backdonation to effectively reverse their intrinsic electrophilicity, thereby enabling the addition to aldehydes and imines stereoselectively. Two distinct transformative pathways for the resultant difluoro π-allylnickel(II) species are developed: exclusively (Z)-defined defluorination and reductive coupling, finally furnishing chiral fluoroalkenyl and gem-difluoro homoallylic derivatives, respectively. In addition, stereodivergent control over vicinal fluorine-containing stereocenters is achievable under the identical catalysis, by simply using geometric isomers of 1-fluorodienes. The current Ni(0)-based umpolung paradigm of fluorodienes establishes a powerful framework for constructing structurally diverse and enantioenriched fluorinated compounds with pharmaceutical significance.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Unilateral
Functionalization of Covalent Organic Frameworks:
Local Electronic Modulation and Morphology-Enabled Mass Transport
for Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production
content:
Abstract
Achieving high selectivity and activity in the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) pathway critically depends on the synergistic modulation of a catalyst’s electronic structure and mass diffusion channels. This work proposes an asymmetric modulation strategy via unilateral functionalization, in which −CH3, −CN, −SO3H, and −NO2 moieties are incorporated into a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs), systematically unraveling the multilevel regulatory mechanisms exerted by functional groups from molecular to macroscopic morphological scales. The research demonstrates that introducing strong electron-withdrawing −NO2 groups can effectively enhance charge transfer at adjacent carbon active sites, reduce the formation barrier of OOH* intermediates, and induce efficient 2e– ORR activity. Concurrently, the polarity and steric effects of functional groups induce structural evolution in COFs from spherical, rod-like to spiderweb-like architectures, wherein the interconnected network of COF-NO2 substantially enhances the diffusion efficiency of reactants and products. This synergy between electronic structure and macroscopic morphology enables COF-NO2 to achieve 94% H2O2 selectivity and a high production rate of 10.5 mol gcat–1 h–1 with sustained stability. This work not only provides outstanding catalysts for efficient electrochemical H2O2 synthesis but also clarifies functional group-induced electronic and morphological modulation, offering a novel paradigm for the rational design of porous catalytic materials.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Autonomous Biogenesis
of Early and Late Assembly Intermediates
of a Large Ribosomal Subunit in a Minimal System
content:
Abstract
Cell-free autonomous biogenesis of ribosomes is important for the bottom-up assembly of an artificial cell and for engineering of functional ribosomes with novel activities. The challenge lies in establishing conditions for a single-step multicomponent synthesis and assembly process in a minimal transcription–translation reaction. We previously reported autonomous synthesis and assembly of a bacterial small ribosomal subunit, but the assembly pathway of the large subunit is more complex with dozens of proteins that bind, fold, and chemically modify its ∼3000-base-long rRNA (rRNA). Here, we cosynthesized all the large subunit components including 33 ribosomal proteins (r-proteins) and 2 rRNAs from DNA brushes and followed the dynamics of assembly coupled to synthesis in real time using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy. A systematic screen of the binding of each of the ribosomal proteins to the 23S rRNA revealed an assembly pattern indicative of early intermediates. The addition of genes coding for six rRNA assembly factors facilitated binding of late assembly ribosomal proteins, supporting formation of late-stage intermediates even in the absence of rRNA modifications. We established a scenario for the large subunit biogenesis via macromolecular colocalization that may aid in the identification and characterization of additional genes required for achieving complete functional ribosome self-regeneration in a minimal system.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
High-Resolution
X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy
of Soluble Methane Monooxygenase: Room Temperature and Cryogenic Insights
into Active Site Electronic Structure Modulation
content:
Abstract
Room temperature HERFD XAS (High Energy Resolution Fluorescence Detected X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy) data collected on the stable Fe(III)Fe(III) (ox) and Fe(II)Fe(II) (red) states of the soluble methane monooxygenase hydroxylase (sMMOH) from Methylosinus trichosporium (Mt) OB3b using laminar flow cells reveal structural differences with varied temperature, pH, and presence of regulatory protein MMOB. High quality room-temperature data on the X-ray radiation sensitive MMOH-ox:MMOB state shows two distinct radiative reduction events, confirming the presence of a so-called semimet (Fe(II)Fe(III)) state in Mt sMMO, and for the first time presents the undamaged HERFD XAS spectra of MMOH-ox and MMOH-ox:MMOB. Clear differences in the whiteline and pre-edge of MMOH-red:MMOB appear between room temperature and cryogenic data, indicating the presence of cryogenic artifacts. In light of this new room temperature data, TD-DFT calculations based on optimized QM/MM models have been used to assign the structures of MMOH-red and ox states. MMOH-red and MMOH-red:MMOB have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate on the basis of pre-edge intensities, with minor perturbations in the ligand field seen upon MMOB binding. MMOH-ox:MMOB and MMOH-ox have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate with different protonation states at pH 7 on the basis of calculated models and changes in the experimental pre-edge energies and intensities for MMOH-ox:MMOB at pH 7.5. Together these results establish a revised structural and mechanistic framework for sMMO and demonstrate the potential of microfluidic HERFD XAS for capturing authentic enzymatic states.

title:
Functionalized Olefin-Linked
Covalent Organic Frameworks
for Selective Mercury Capture and Recovery from Vinyl Chloride-Rich
Gas Streams
content:
Abstract
The calcium carbide-derived acetylene hydrochlorination route for vinyl chloride monomer (VCM, C2H3Cl) production remains a major source of mercury consumption and emission owing to its reliance on HgCl2/activated carbon catalysts. Selective removal of elemental mercury (Hg0) from crude VCM streams is intrinsically challenging because Hg0 must be captured from C2H3Cl-rich and HCl-containing atmospheres without coadsorbing valuable C2H3Cl. Here, we report a pore-engineered covalent organic framework (COF) platform in which olefin-linked sp2-carbon-conjugated frameworks suppress nonspecific C2H3Cl adsorption, while Cu-coordinated 2-(methylthio)ethoxy side chains create well-defined Cu–O2S2 pockets for selective Hg0 capture. These structural features afford an ideal adsorbed solution theory-predicted Hg0/C2H3Cl selectivity exceeding 20,000. Notably, dynamic breakthrough experiments under simulated industrial conditions containing 5 vol % HCl further revealed a Hg0 breakthrough time of over 10,000 min g–1 in C2H3Cl-rich streams, with a separation factor of approximately 52, demonstrating exceptional resistance to acid-induced deactivation. Treatment of the spent adsorbent with Na2S solution enables regeneration over 30 consecutive cycles and converts captured mercury into chemically stable HgS. This work establishes a molecularly precise removal–recovery platform for elemental mercury from chemically complex industrial gas streams, highlighting the power of programmed pore microenvironments to discriminate trace toxic species from abundant value-added molecules under chemically aggressive conditions.

title:
Asymmetric Alkylation
of α-Cyanoketimines
with Alkyl Bromides Catalyzed by Bis-Cinchonium Salts
content:
Abstract
The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides. This reaction features a broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby providing a useful approach to enantioenriched α,α-dialkyl aminonitriles. Computational studies revealed that the bis-cinchonium catalyst, through a network of weak bonding interactions, activated both cyanoketimines and alkyl bromides and preorganized them along the trajectory toward the transition state of an SN2 reaction.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Solar Biorefinery:
Stoichiometric Coproduction of
Gluconic and Glucaric Acids and Impurity-Free Hydrogen from Lignocellulosic
Biomass and Water
content:
Abstract
Solar biorefinery serves as a game changer in the sustainable production of transportation fuels and value-added chemicals by capitalizing on sunlight, lignocellulosic biomass, and water. Central to this endeavor is the modulation of highly reactive, nonselective hydroxyl radicals to prevent undesired side reactions. Here, surface-hydroxylated nickel oxyphosphide works synergistically with one-dimensional gallium nitride, enabling the selective reforming of lignocellulose in water toward glucose-derived organic acids (GOAs: gluconic and glucaric acids) and H2 at a nearly stoichiometric ratio: (C6H12O6)n+ H2O + sunlight → GOAs + H2. The GaN@NiOP–OH system achieves an H2 evolution rate of 2.55 mol g–1 h–1 with 100% gas-phase selectivity under simulated concentrated sunlight at 3.5 W cm–2. GOAs are simultaneously produced at a total rate of 2.23 mol g–1 h–1, corresponding to a near-stoichiometric GOAs/H2 ratio of 0.97 with nearly 100% atom utilization efficiency. This platform is broadly applicable to sunlight-driven reforming of cellulose, straw, and camphorwood. In situ spectroscopy, isotope labeling, and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that NiOP–OH cooperates with GaN to modulate in situ-generated hydroxyl radical species originating from water oxidation by photogenerated holes. These radicals are confined on the catalytic surface with their nonselective reactivity finely tuned, enabling selective conversion of glucose with H2O into GOAs and H2 via a dynamic hydroxyl exchange mechanism while suppressing side and mineralization reactions. Outdoor testing and techno-economic analysis confirm the practical viability of this proof-of-concept solar biorefinery for coproducing high-value chemicals and green H2 using only sunlight, lignocellulose, and water.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
High-Resolution  6 Li Solid-State Nuclear
Magnetic Resonance Reveals Hidden Lithium Dynamics in All-Solid-State
Cathodes
content:
Abstract
The decisive chemistry of iron-based halide cathodes─where lithium resides, how it evolves, and how disorder governs multielectron redox─has remained largely inaccessible, limiting the rational design of catholyte-free composite cathodes in all-solid-state lithium batteries. Here we make the lithium sublattice directly visible in paramagnetic LiFeCl3 using a 6Li solid-state NMR strategy combining high isotopic enrichment, optimized acquisition, and variable-temperature control. This method resolves and quantifies three Li+ environments, revealing that local Li/Fe disorder drives in-place Fe2+ reduction as the root cause of highly reversible intercalation-conversion chemistry. It further uncovers trace irreversible Fe0 species invisible to conventional spectroscopic and imaging techniques. Guided by this hidden degradation signature, optimization of the voltage window enables 85.9% capacity retention after 500 cycles with a 16.3% energy-density penalty, whereas full-depth cycling retains 68.6% after 100 cycles. Our work establishes lithium-resolved NMR as a platform linking disorder, hidden redox, and reversibility in paramagnetic cathodes.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Photocatalytic Three-Component
Radical Addition of
Aromatic Compounds
content:
Abstract
Substitution dominates benzene chemistry because σ-adducts formed during bond construction usually rearomatize. We report a photocatalytic three-component reaction that retains the σ-adduct as a 1,4-dioxygenated cyclohexadiene. A highly reactive carbonyloxy radical adds to the arene, whereas a longer lived peroxyl radical intercepts the resulting cyclohexadienyl radical before rearomatization. A reactivity–polarity analysis rationalizes the distinct requirements for entry and capture, and time-resolved electron paramagnetic resonance detects cyclohexadienyl and tert-butylperoxyl radicals under related conditions. The reaction extends to substituted, fused, and electron-rich heteroarenes and provides benzene-derived intermediates that can be converted to hydroquinone, conduritols, and inositol isomers. These results establish kinetic differentiation of radical partners as a strategy for controlling the fate of arene σ-adducts.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
Visualizing
B–N Bond Breaking in Silicone Elastomer
Networks through Turn-On Mechanochromic Luminescence
content:
Abstract
Mechanochromic luminescence (MCL) plays important roles in sensors, encryption, as impact indicators, and in real-time stress mapping. Boron–nitrogen Lewis pairs (LPs) are promising as mechanophores because both the interaction energy and the luminescence color can be readily fine-tuned. However, elastomers based on luminescent organoboron polymers have yet to be explored. Mechanofluorochromic elastomers were prepared by cross-linking pyridyl-substituted poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) with luminescent polystyrene (PS)-based organoborane polymeric Lewis acids. Apart from enabling the full compatibilization of otherwise immiscible PS/PDMS matrices, supramolecular B–N bond formation quenched the blue emission of PS1 via complexation of its pendant bithiophenyl-substituted arylborane chromophore units with pyridyl-functionalized PDMS. Upon stretching of the polymer film, a fluorescence turn-on, corresponding to uncomplexed boron chromophores, was observed by the naked eye under UV irradiation, indicating that the mechanical force was effectively translated to cleave the dynamic B–N bond. Aided by the low Tg of the PDMS segments, the “frustrated” mechanofluorochromic Lewis pairs (MFLPs) recombined instantly upon stress relief, rendering the material nonfluorescent again. Use of a yellow-luminescent donor-π-acceptor fluorophore that turns blue-emissive after pyridyl binding in PS2 led to a ratiometric fluorescence response. Tensile tests and oscillatory rheology studies showed that network F1 was relatively stronger than network F2, consistent with the relative Lewis acid strengths and ligand exchange kinetics derived from studies on molecular model systems. These results demonstrate the potential of tunable B–N Lewis pairs as versatile mechanofluorochromic cross-links in polymer networks.

title:
A Pyridoxal
5′-Phosphate-Dependent Decarboxylative
Mannich Reaction Initiates Construction of the Nonpeptidic Scaffold
of Kaitocephalin
content:
Abstract
Kaitocephalin (KCP) is a fungal neuroactive natural product bearing a peptide-like yet nonpeptidic amino acid-derived scaffold in which amino acid-like units are connected by C–C bonds rather than peptide bonds. The enzymatic construction of this unusual scaffold has remained unresolved. Here, we identify KpbH as a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme that couples pyrroline-5-carboxylate, generated from l-ornithine, with l-aspartate to form (2S,5R)-5-[(S)-2-amino-2-carboxyethyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (ACPCA), which corresponds to the nonpeptidic Ala–Pro substructure of KCP. D2O-labeling experiments showed enzyme-controlled, solvent-derived deuterium incorporation at C7 of ACPCA, supporting a decarboxylative Mannich-type mechanism. Feeding of a deuterium-enriched ACPCA-containing reaction mixture to the KCP-producing fungus Eupenicillium shearii resulted in deuterium incorporation into KCP, linking ACPCA to KCP biosynthesis. These results identify KpbH as the first native PLP-dependent enzyme that catalyzes an l-aspartate-dependent decarboxylative Mannich-type C–C bond-forming reaction and reveal a biosynthetic strategy for constructing a noncanonical amino acid-like C–C bond scaffold.

title: Redefining the thermal safety boundaries of ether-based sodium batteries
content: Are ether electrolytes inherently hazardous? This perspective reveals they actually deliver markedly enhanced thermal safety over carbonates in sodium architectures alongside uniquely higher thermal resilience toward metallic sodium than lithium equivalents. However, this protective margin is fundamentally negated by oxygen-driven chemical autoxidation rather than mere electrochemical degradation. These insights establish the anode-free ether configuration as the definitive trajectory for future sodium batteries, perfectly balancing energy density with robust safety.

title:
Synergistic
Promotion of Methane Hydrate Formation
by  l -Tryptophan and PCN-250-Fe 2 Co for Efficient
Hydrate-Based Separation of Low-Concentration Coalbed Methane
content:
Abstract
Hydrate-based separation is an effective method for CH4 recovery from low-concentration coalbed methane. The hydrate separation performance, such as the generation rate and the efficiency of separation and purification, is influenced by kinetic promoters. In this work, a dual-promoter system consisting of l-tryptophan (l-Trp) and PCN-250-Fe2Co was developed to enhance hydrate-based CH4 separation. l-Trp regulates the gas–liquid interfacial microenvironment through its amphiphilic structure, suppressing compact ice crystal nucleation and enhancing CH4 diffusive transport across the interface. Meanwhile, the high specific surface area and abundant microporous structure of PCN-250-Fe2Co provide numerous heterogeneous nucleation sites for CH4, shorten the CH4 diffusion distance, and significantly enhance the mass transfer within the liquid phase. As a result, the optimized system containing 0.5 wt % l-Trp and 0.1 wt % PCN-250-Fe2Co framework achieved a CH4 recovery of 86.64%. This value is 11.46% and 5.02% higher than those obtained with PCN-250-Fe2Co alone and l-Trp alone, respectively. This significant enhancement is attributable to the synergistic interplay between the carboxylate anchors of l-Trp and the metal sites of PCN-250-Fe2Co, which simultaneously facilitate CH4 capture and mitigate mass-transfer resistance for CH4. Theoretical analysis further showed that the CH4/N2 selective adsorption ratio of the l-Trp&PCN-250-Fe2Co system (44.932) was 16.6% higher than that of the PCN-250-Fe2Co system (38.523). Overall, the l-Trp&PCN-250-Fe2Co composite system exhibits promising potential for hydrate-based CH4 separation and purification from low-concentration coalbed methane, providing a new method for hydrate-based gas separation.

title:
Influence
of a Nanoparticle-Enhanced Gemini VES Fracturing
Fluid on Methane Adsorption Characteristics of Coal
content:
Abstract
To elucidate the effect of a nanoparticle-synergistic Gemini VES (NPs-Gemini VES) fracturing fluid on methane adsorption in coal, coal samples were immersed in the SiO2 nanoparticle-enhanced Gemini VES fracturing fluid for different time durations. The changes in the methane adsorption behavior were evaluated using a magnetic suspension balance. On the basis of the experimental results, a coal–NPs-Gemini VES model was constructed in Materials Studio (MS), and grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations were performed to investigate methane adsorption capacity, adsorption configurations, and intermolecular interaction energies. The molecular interactions among coal, fracturing fluid components, and methane were analyzed to clarify their competitive adsorption behavior on the coal surface. The results indicate that all fracturing fluid systems suppressed methane adsorption, with the greatest reduction observed for the NPs-Gemini VES treatment. At 0.5 MPa, methane adsorption decreased by 20.87% and 34.15% after 24 and 96 h of treatment, respectively, whereas the reductions in the other systems plateaued after 24 h. At 2 MPa, the electrostatic interaction energies of the coal–Gemini VES and coal–NPs-Gemini VES systems were 31.96% and 49.22% higher, respectively, than those of the coal–water system, enabling the Gemini VES-SiO2 composite structure to preferentially occupy high-energy adsorption sites. Furthermore, the interconnected composite network formed by the NPs-Gemini VES fracturing fluid occupied the effective adsorption space available for methane and enhanced interfacial water occupancy by modifying the interfacial properties, resulting in methane adsorption at the remaining low-energy adsorption sites with reduced adsorption stability. These effects substantially weakened the methane adsorption capacity of the coal.

title:
Upcycling
Hazardous Industrial Waste into Chlorinated
Sorbents toward Cost-Effective Mercury Removal from Syngas
content:
Abstract
Mercury-containing spent catalyst (MCSC) from acetylene hydrochlorination and acidic cupric etchants from printed-circuit-board manufacture are hazardous wastes that retain a porous carbon scaffold and reactive chloride species. Herein, their detoxification and reuse were coupled to produce a chlorine-functionalized carbon sorbent for gaseous elemental mercury (Hg0) capture from syngas. Residual mercury in MCSC was first recovered by thermal desorption, producing mercury-free spent catalyst (MFSC) with a preserved hierarchical porous structure. MFSC was then treated by one-step in situ etching with spent acid (SA), activated by H+, Cu2+, and Cl– components to exert its function. The optimized 20SA-MFSC achieved 99.8% Hg0 removal efficiency within 60 min at 100 °C and maintained >95% Hg0 removal for 8 h under pure N2. In the long-term breakthrough test, the cumulative Hg0 adsorption capacity reached 10.42 mg·g–1 at an outlet-to-inlet Hg0 concentration ratio of 0.8. Mechanism analysis implicated that Cl-containing species, especially surface chloride and covalent C–Cl groups, dominated Hg0 removal by converting Hg0 into HgCl2 species. Techno-economic and life cycle assessments demonstrated that the waste-derived route reduced estimated production cost, global warming potential, and cumulative energy demand by 90.9%, 48.1%, and 63.0%, respectively, relative to a commercial-reagent route. These benefits primarily arose from replacing commercial activated carbon and reagents with waste-derived feedstocks, while residual mercury recovery provided a byproduct credit that partially offset the processing costs. This work provides a sustainable and synergistic route integrating hazardous-waste detoxification, resource utilization, and Hg0 pollution control.

title: Ammonium Ion Intercalation Enabled Stable 1T-VS 2 /WS 2 -Nb 2 CT x  Heterostructures during Electrochemical Charge Storage
content:
Abstract
The performance of energy storage devices utilizing multilayered materials is governed by the complex interactions between electrolyte ions and the electrode. Consequently, inhibiting the irreversible oxidative failure of the electrodes is crucial. Herein, an in situ modification strategy that introduces NH4+ species in Nb2CTx MXene electrodes and integrates them with 1T phase VS2/WS2 heteronanosheets is evaluated. The resulting VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+ electrodes demonstrate a specific capacity of up to 217.48 mA h g–1 at 1 A g–1 with excellent electrochemical stability at high current densities. Density functional theory simulations confirmed the strong electronic interaction between the NH4+-intercalated Nb2CTx and 1T-WS2/VS2 nanosheets, resulting in higher OH– adsorption energies. Operando Raman analysis revealed that the process involves cation dehydration and K+ rehydration. These results highlight the importance of NH4+ dynamics, thermodynamic stability, and interfacial interactions. A VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+//N-doped nanocube-based asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated, exhibiting a peak energy density of 54 Wh kg–1 and long-term cycling stability without significant performance degradation.

title: Fast, Hybrid Perovskite Deposition via Gas Flow Assisted Single Source Flash Evaporation
content:
Abstract
A large number of publications, using diverse production techniques, are demonstrating the potential of metal halide perovskite thin-film devices. Promising records in power conversion efficiencies, device lifetimes and photo-electrical applications have been reported worldwide. A simple and rapid deposition method, however, is still missing. This work introduces a possible answer: Gas Flow Assisted Flash Evaporation (Gas-FE). Gas-FE is a solvent-free deposition method operating under modest vacuum conditions that enables the deposition of complex perovskites with components having varying vapor pressures. We demonstrate its capabilities by subliming complex powder compositions relevant for perovskite photovoltaics and show a proof-of-concept methylammonium lead iodide-based (MAPbI3) solar cell containing methylammonium chloride and lithium TFSI as dopants. Growth rates exceeding 1 µm/min are obtained for crystalline, highly oriented perovskite films with good optical and electronic properties. The perovskite film is integrated into a fully vacuum-deposited p-i-n photovoltaic device, yielding a promising power conversion efficiency of 9.6%.

title: Influences of Nanostructuring and Densification Processes on the Lattice Thermal Conductivity of  n -Type Indium Antimonide
content:
Abstract
Indium antimonide (InSb), an n-type narrow-band gap semiconductor, has attracted considerable interest in intermediate-temperature thermoelectric (TE) applications due to its excellent electronic transport properties; however, its relatively high lattice thermal conductivity limits its TE performance. Here, we explore the effects of mechanical milling and densification techniques on the structural, vibrational, thermoelectric, and mechanical properties of InSb prepared by the solid-state melting route, then ball-milled and densified via resistive hot-press (RHP) and induction-assisted hot-press (IHP). Phase identification and microstructural analyses of InSb have been examined by powder X-ray diffraction and electron probe microanalysis. Mechanical milling drastically reduces the crystallite size, suppresses the lattice thermal conductivity (κlat) through enhanced phonon scattering, and decreases electrical conductivity due to reduced carrier mobility. Further, the milled samples densified by RHP and IHP have shown ultralow κlat values of ∼3.46 and ∼4.69 W m–1 K–1 at 300 K, respectively, illustrating reductions of ∼50% and ∼47% compared to bulk RHP and IHP samples. The maximum zT of ∼0.38 at 723 K was obtained for bulk RHP, along with a high mechanical hardness of 2.14 GPa, implying that InSb is a potential n-type candidate for intermediate-temperature TE applications.

title: Hybrid Supercapacitor Based on Functionalized Ni-MOF Composite: Achieving Superior Power Density in Asymmetric Energy Storage Device
content:
Abstract
Hybrid energy storage systems have gained significant attention for addressing rising global energy demands by combining the complementary strengths of batteries and supercapacitors. Their practical implementation, however, requires simultaneous achievement of high energy and power densities, long-term cycling stability, and robust capacitance retention, criteria often limited by the inadequate functionality and structural instability of conventional electrode materials. In this work, a bromine-functionalized nickel-based MOF (Ni-HBTM) containing free carboxylic acid groups was synthesized to overcome these limitations. The Ni-HBTM metal–organic framework (MOF) delivered a specific capacitance of 620.22 F/g at 1 A/g in an alkaline electrolyte. When integrated with reduced graphene oxide (Ni-HBTM@rGO_20), the composite achieved an impressive specific capacitance of 1237.3 F/g at 1 A/g. An asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) assembled using Ni-HBTM@rGO_20 as the positive electrode exhibited a specific capacitance of 174.04 F/g, energy density of 54.39 Wh/kg at 1 A/g, and a power density of 11,250 W/kg at 15 A/g current densities with 94% capacitance retention after 10,000 cycles, which is a significantly high specific capacitance and power density for Ni-MOF-based composites in comparable conditions. The ASC successfully powered light-emitting diodes (LEDs), demonstrating the potential of functionalized MOF-based materials to bridge the performance gap between batteries and supercapacitors and offering an approach toward next-generation all-solid-state energy storage devices.

title: Three-Dimensional Porous Silicon-Carbon Polymorph: Li/Na Functionalization toward High-Efficiency Hydrogen Storage
content:
Abstract
Porous materials decorated with alkali metals have emerged as attractive candidates for reversible hydrogen storage because they can simultaneously provide high adsorption capacity, suitable adsorption strength, and rapid hydrogen transport. Motivated by this strategy, the present work explores the hydrogen-storage behavior of three-dimensional porous silicon-carbon polymorph 3D-t(SiC)12 after Li and Na functionalization using density functional theory (DFT) calculations together with ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. Both alkali metals interact strongly with the host framework, exhibiting binding energies of –2.58 eV for Li and –2.10 eV for Na, which indicates thermodynamically stable decoration and minimizes the tendency toward metal clustering. A clear distinction is observed between the two decorating species, with Li producing significantly stronger interactions with hydrogen molecules than Na. As a result, the Li-functionalized framework stores as many as 34 H2 molecules, corresponding to a gravimetric capacity of 6.39 wt %, while maintaining an average adsorption energy of –0.167 eV per H2, a value favorable for reversible adsorption and desorption. Under identical conditions, Na decoration yields a lower storage capacity of 5.86 wt %. Thermodynamic calculations predict hydrogen release within an average temperature window of 267–368 K and equilibrium pressures between 8 and 20 bar, highlighting practical operating conditions. Dynamic stability is confirmed by AIMD simulations, which show that the hydrogenated structures remain intact throughout the simulations while preserving reversible adsorption characteristics. In addition, hydrogen diffusion on the Li-decorated surface proceeds through remarkably small activation barriers of only 0.010–0.178 eV, suggesting highly efficient molecular transport across the porous network. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that Li-functionalized 3D-t(SiC)12 is a highly promising solid-state hydrogen-storage material and provide valuable design principles for next-generation porous hydrogen-storage materials.

title: Enhancing the Hydrogen Evolution Activity of Ni-Based Electrocatalysts Through Codoping of Chromium and Molybdenum
content:
Abstract
Electrochemical water splitting represents an alternative method for producing molecular hydrogen, a promising clean energy alternative to fossil fuels. Ni-based alloys have received increased attention as earth-abundant catalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), where performance can be optimized through alloying with heteroatoms. Herein, we report an integrated theoretical and experimental study that elucidates the effects of Cr and Mo doping on the HER activity and stability of Ni1–xCrx, Ni1–yMoy, and Ni1–x–yCrxMoy alloy nanocrystals (NCs). Theoretical calculations predicted that codoping of Cr/Mo can significantly enhance the HER activity of Ni, as evidenced by more favorable hydrogen binding free energies (|ΔGH|) achieved for Ni1–x–yCrxMoy alloys. Accordingly, a series of binary and ternary alloys were colloidally synthesized to investigate the composition-dependent HER activity in alkaline electrolytes. Morphological analysis of Ni1–xCrx and Ni1–yMoy NCs revealed average sizes of 10.2 ± 2.0 and 13.4 ± 2.8 nm, respectively while Ni1–x–yCrxMoy alloys showed significantly larger (33.3 ± 8.9 – 37.4 ± 17.6 nm) diameters. Nonetheless, the cubic structure of parent Ni NCs was retained upon codoping of Cr/Mo. Surface analysis revealed prominent variations in surface chemistry, leading to a shift of electron density from Ni toward Cr and Mo. HER performance revealed a volcano trend in electrocatalytic activity with Ni0.914Cr0.057Mo0.029 composition displaying the highest activity, which is comparable to Pt/C standard (10% wt) at a current density (j) of –10 mA/cm2. Despite all alloys displaying Volmer-influenced HER kinetics, simultaneous admixing of 5.7% Cr and 2.9% Mo produced the lowest Tafel slope (80 mV/dec), suggesting enhanced catalytic activity for the optimally doped composition. The codoping of Cr/Mo substantially improved the charge transfer resistance, electrochemically active surface area, and short-term stability of alloys in alkali. This study advances our understanding of the composition-dependent HER activity of Ni-based alloys and demonstrates how computationally guided doping strategies can be utilized to produce high-efficiency and earth-abundant catalysts for water electrolysis.

title: Energy Storage across Scales: Bridging Material Design and System-Level Performance
MOF-Supported Pt-Alloy Electrocatalysts for Oxygen Reduction Reaction in PEM Fuel Cells: Design, Performance, and Future Directions
content:
Abstract
Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) are promising energy conversion technologies for transportation, portable power, and stationary energy applications because of their high efficiency and low emissions. However, the widespread commercialization of PEMFCs remains limited by the high cost and long-term durability challenges of platinum (Pt)-based oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysts. In recent years, metal–organic framework (MOF)-derived materials have emerged as attractive catalyst supports owing to their tunable porosity, high surface area, controllable composition, and ability to generate conductive heteroatom-doped carbon architectures. These characteristics provide opportunities to improve catalyst dispersion, Pt utilization, mass transport, and catalyst stability under fuel-cell operating conditions. This review summarizes recent advances in MOF-supported Pt-alloy electrocatalysts for the ORR in PEMFCs, with emphasis on Pt–Co, Pt–Fe, and Pt–Ni catalyst systems. The effects of MOF-derived supports on catalyst structure, metal–support interactions, catalytic activity, and durability are critically discussed. Particular attention is given to the relationships between support architecture, alloy composition, ORR performance, and fuel-cell-relevant stability. In addition, current challenges associated with transition-metal dissolution, catalyst degradation, large-scale synthesis, and practical PEMFC implementation are examined. Finally, future opportunities for the design of MOF-derived catalyst supports and durable, high-performance Pt-alloy electrocatalysts are highlighted to accelerate the development of economically viable PEMFC technologies.

title: Bulk Electronic Transformations in Si–Ge Alloys during Lithiation Probed by Si L 2,3 -edge X-ray Raman Scattering
content:
Abstract
Silicon–germanium alloys are promising high-capacity anode materials for lithium-ion batteries, yet their lithiation mechanisms remain only partially understood due to the limitations of conventional characterization techniques. In this work, Si L2,3-edge X-ray Raman scattering (XRS) is combined with Finite Difference Method Near Edge Structure (FDMNES) multiple-scattering calculations to investigate micron/submicron ball-milled and nanosized laser-pyrolyzed Si0.5Ge0.5 electrodes during the first lithiation cycle. Explicit SiGe and Li-rich Si–Ge structural models reveal a pronounced influence of Ge on the Si L2,3-edge line shape in the pristine state, whereas this effect becomes much less evident after lithiation. The Li-rich spectra of both materials are consistently described using the Li15(SiGe)4 model, while the different effective screening values required for BM and LP are interpreted as model-dependent descriptors of their local electronic environments rather than as quantitative measures of charge transfer. The broad intensity observed in the 103–109 eV region is consistent with overlapping contributions of the alloy electronic structure and oxidized Si environments, rather than being attributable to a unique lithiated species. These results demonstrate that Si L2,3-edge XRS, supported by explicit alloy modeling, provides a bulk-sensitive probe of electronic transformations in Si–Ge anodes and highlights the combined influence of alloying, morphology, and lithiation on the Si electronic response.

title: Atomic-Layer-Deposited Interlayers Enabling Interfacial Band Tuning in Vapor Transport Deposition-SnS/CdS Solar Cells
content:
Abstract
Severe interfacial recombination remains a key barrier limiting carrier collection in SnS thin-film solar cells. Thus, in this study, atomic layer deposition (ALD)-based thin oxide interlayers are engineered at the SnS/CdS heterojunction. The applicability of ZnO, SnO2, and zinc tin oxide (ZTO) interlayers was probed to understand the interfacial electronic structure by systematically controlling the ALD process. The optimized condition within the investigated parameter range, corresponding to a 15 nm ZTO interlayer deposited at 120 °C, provides favorable interfacial band alignment, striking a balance between low transport resistance and favorable band alignment. The resulting SnS/ALD-ZTO/CdS solar cell achieved a power conversion efficiency of 4.45% (VOC = 0.326 V, JSC = 24.50 mA cm–2, FF = 56%), outperforming the 3.72% (VOC = 0.325 V, JSC = 21.30 mA cm–2, FF = 54%) baseline device without interlayer modification. UPS and XPS analyses confirm that 120 °C processing promotes favorable band offsets at the heterointerface governed by the well-coordinated Zn–Sn–O chemical environment. Dark J–V measurements support suppressed recombination, as evidenced by an approximately 2.4-fold reduction in the J0. This work demonstrates ALD-ZTO as an effective interface-engineering approach for high-performance SnS solar cells.

title: Synergistic Crystal Facet Engineering and Bi Incorporation in ZnIn 2 S 4  for Enhanced Photocatalytic CO 2  Reduction
content:
Abstract
Crystal facet engineering and Bi incorporation are effective strategies to enhance photocatalytic CO2 reduction, yet their synergistic effects in ZnIn2S4 remain underexplored. Herein, Bi-modified ZnIn2S4 (Bi-ZIS) with a preferentially exposed (006) plane and enriched sulfur vacancies (VS) was constructed via a combined crystal facet engineering and Bi-doping strategy. The optimized 5% Bi-ZIS exhibited the highest photocatalytic performance, producing CO and CH4 yields of 242 and 45 μmol g–1 under visible-light irradiation for 3 h. Comprehensive characterizations revealed that the exposed (006) plane, sulfur vacancies, and Bi nanoparticles collectively promoted light harvesting, charge separation, and CO2 activation. In situ DRIFTS confirmed the presence of key intermediates (*COOH, CHO*, CH3O*), and DFT calculations verified electronic-structure modulation induced by Bi doping. This work provides an efficient strategy for rational design of ZnIn2S4-based photocatalysts via synergistic crystal facet and defect engineering for solar-driven CO2 conversion.

title: Spontaneous Formation of a Li–Al Oxide Coating Layer on Ni-Rich Positive Electrode Materials and Improvement of Electrochemical Performance
content:
Abstract
Surface coating with a lithium-ion conductor is an effective strategy for improving the electrochemical performance of positive electrode materials for lithium-ion batteries. However, preparing a uniform coating by a simple, cost-effective, and solvent-free process remains challenging. Here, we show that simply mixing Ni-rich LiNi0.85Mn0.10Co0.05O2 (NMC) positive electrode material with Al2O3 nanoparticles (NPs) causes the residual alkali species on the NMC surface to spontaneously react with the Al2O3 NPs, forming a Li–Al oxide layer and thereby improving the electrochemical performance of Ni-rich NMC. Full-cell tests at 45 °C showed that 0.25 wt % Al2O3 NPs markedly improved capacity retention, particularly at high rates. pH titration and hard X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed that residual LiOH reacted with Al2O3 NPs to form Li–Al oxides on the NMC surface before cycling. This indicates a spontaneous reaction between Al2O3 NPs and residual LiOH during dry mixing. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy mapping further revealed that a thin Al-rich layer a few nanometers thick was formed even on surface regions distant from the Al2O3 NPs, suggesting that the Al2O3 NPs reacted with LiOH distributed across the entire NMC surface, thereby forming a nanoscale coating layer. Postmortem scanning transmission electron microscopy coupled with electron energy-loss spectroscopy analysis confirmed a reduced NiO-like rock-salt layer after cycling, indicating that the self-formed Li–Al oxide layer suppresses surface degradation. This solvent-free coating approach offers a simple, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly route for improving the electrochemical performance of Ni-rich NMC.

title: Unveiling Bulk Carrier Transport in LiTaGeO 5  and NaTaGeO 5  Photocatalysts through Integrated Crystal and Electronic Structure Analyses
content:
Abstract
The rational design of semiconductor photocatalysts with efficient bulk charge separation remains a major challenge for solar energy conversion. Herein, titanite-type LiTaGeO5 (LTGO) and NaTaGeO5 (NTGO) are investigated as model systems to elucidate how crystal structures and electronic structures govern carrier transport behavior in oxide semiconductors. Structural analyses reveal that both compounds contain quasi-one-dimensional [TaO6] octahedral chains separated by [GeO4] tetrahedra and alkali-metal cations. The substitution of local structural adjustments induces distinct local structural rearrangements within the framework while preserving the overall chain-like connectivity. Electronic structure and chemical bonding analyses demonstrate that the valence band maximum (VBM) is dominated by nonbonding O 2p orbitals, whereas the conduction band minimum (CBM) is contributed by Ta 5d–O 2p and Ge 4s–O 2s antibonding orbitals, revealing that the frontier electronic states involve multiple structural units rather than solely the [TaO6] chains. Nevertheless, both compounds exhibit preferential carrier transport along the [TaO6] chain direction due to the anisotropic connectivity of frontier-orbital-contributing structural units. Under UV irradiation, Pd-loaded LTGO and NTGO achieve hydrogen evolution rates of 36.7(4) and 59.6(3) μmol/h, respectively, with NTGO exhibiting superior photocatalytic performance. This work demonstrates that the spatial connectivity of frontier-orbital-contributing structural units, together with local structural modulation and chemical bonding characteristics, is crucial for understanding bulk carrier transport and photocatalytic behavior in oxide semiconductors.

title: A Retrospective Benchmark of Quantitative Antimicrobial Peptide Activity Prediction Tools
content:
Ten publicly released antimicrobial peptide minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) prediction tools are retrospectively evaluated on a recent‐literature external benchmark. Absolute MIC regression performance is generally limited, whereas selected tools retain useful ranking and virtual‐screening enrichment. The benchmark further identifies residue‐associated error patterns.








ABSTRACT
Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are critical candidates for addressing the global antibiotic resistance crisis. AI‐driven quantitative models capable of directly predicting peptide antimicrobial activity, specifically minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), are gaining scientific prominence by providing precise guidance for the rational design of AMPs. To assess their real‐world, out‐of‐the‐box performance, we conducted a retrospective benchmark of 10 publicly released quantitative AMP prediction tools spanning classical machine learning and contemporary deep learning approaches. Using an external dataset and reconstructed native datasets, we evaluated absolute MIC regression, retrospective reproducibility, directional prediction patterns, ranking capability, and virtual‐screening enrichment. Most released tools exhibited poor absolute MIC regression and limited transferability to the external benchmark, while selected tools retained useful relative‐ranking and enrichment capabilities. Retrospective evaluation further revealed marked differences in implementation‐level reproducibility among the released tools. Error‐stratified analyses identified systematic associations between prediction errors and peptide residue composition, together with a general compression of the predicted activity range. Collectively, these findings characterize the practical performance boundaries of currently accessible quantitative AMP prediction tools and support their use primarily as early‐stage screening filters rather than precise substitutes for experimental MIC measurements.

title: Interlayer‐Engineered 1T‐MoSe2 Enabling Reversible Mn2+/H+ Hybrid Storage for Aqueous Manganese Batteries
content:
Phase‐engineered 1T MoSe2 with expanded interlayer spacing enables fast and reversible Mn2+/H+ co‐intercalation, delivering long‐life and high‐performance aqueous manganese batteries.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous manganese batteries are emerging as safe, low‐cost options for large‐scale energy storage but are limited by sluggish Mn2+ diffusion and poor reversibility. Here, we report an interlayer‐engineered 1T‐phase MoSe2 cathode enabling fast, reversible hybrid storage of Mn2+ and H+ ions. Controlled chemical exfoliation induces a metallic phase transition and expands the interlayer spacing, creating a favorable environment for multivalent ion transport. The exfoliated MoSe2 delivers 153.4 mAh g−1 at 0.1 A g−1 and retains 92.5% capacity after 1800 cycles. Kinetic analysis shows a reduced ion migration barrier compared with bulk MoSe2, highlighting the role of phase engineering and interlayer expansion. Spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses reveal a reversible Mn2+/H+ co‐intercalation mechanism. A full cell paired with a Mn metal anode delivers 165.3 mAh g−1 and retains 89.9% of its capacity after 2000 cycles, demonstrating the practical feasibility of a rechargeable aqueous Mn‐metal battery. This work establishes phase‐engineered layered dichalcogenides as a platform for aqueous multivalent batteries and provides design principles to overcome kinetic limitations.

title: Cooperative Bulk‐Interface Regulation Through Na/F/Al Functional Synergy Enables Structural and Interfacial Stability in Li‐Rich Layered Oxides
content:
Cooperative Na/F/Al regulation simultaneously tunes the layered lattice and surface chemistry of Li‐rich layered oxides, enabling stabilized Mn‐O coordination, suppressed structural degradation, and enhanced Li+ transport. The resulting cathode delivers high‐rate capability and durable cycling, revealing a synergistic bulk interface stabilization strategy for high‐performance Li‐rich layered oxide cathodes.








ABSTRACT
Lithium rich manganese layered oxides (LRMs) are promising cathode materials for high energy lithium‐ion batteries owing to their high capacity and low cost, yet their practical applications are limited by lattice degradation and unstable cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI) evolution during cycling. Herein, a fluorine enriched multifunctional Li1.2Mn0.54Ni0.13Co0.13O2(LRM) is constructed through Na+, F−, and Al3+ synergistic regulation to achieve bulk surface stabilization. The introduction of Na+ broadens Li interlayer spacing and accelerates Li+ transport, while Al‐O bonding stabilizes the local electronic structure, suppresses cation disorder and Jahn‐Teller distortion, and alleviates lattice strain. Furthermore, the preformed fluorine enriched surface region reinforces the outer lattice through the formation of robust F‐TM bonds, promoting the generation of a uniform and stable CEI layer, mitigating electrolyte decomposition and interfacial reactions. The optimized NFA‐LRM delivers a high discharge capacity of 318.7 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C, with reversible capacities of 140.6 and 108.5 mAh g−1 at 5 C and 10 C, respectively, and retains 96.29% capacity after 250 cycles at 2 C. This work provides a bulk and surface synergistic strategy for high energy LRMs with stabilized oxygen chemistry and durable interfacial stability.

title:
Supramolecular Mask-Mediated
Regioselective bis-Bingel-Functionalization
of M 3 N@I  h  -C 80  (M = Lu, Sc)
content:
Abstract
Exohedral functionalization of endohedral metallofullerenes (EMFs) is essential for exploiting these intriguing molecules as novel materials in applications such as biomedicine and organic solar cell device design. In the case of trimetallic nitride template EMFs (TNT-EMFs), many functionalization methods effective for empty fullerenes are inaccessible or less efficient due to the presence of the encapsulated cluster. This inner cluster increases the electron density on the carbon cage surface, reducing its reactivity. Moreover, it has been demonstrated that the inner cluster controls both the reactivity and regioselectivity of bare TNT-EMFs. The supramolecular mask strategy (SMS) has yielded promising results in the functionalization of C60 and C70 and, for the first time, is applied here to endohedral fullerenes to achieve mono- and bis-functionalization of Lu3N@Ih-C80 and Sc3N@Ih-C80. Encapsulation of both TNT-EMFs within a tetragonal prismatic cage host is crucial for enhancing their reactivity, enabling bis-functionalization under milder conditions and with shorter reaction times. Comprehensive spectroscopic and spectrometric characterization, combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, identified the most favorable and stable bis-adducts by considering the positive alignment between the geometry imposed by the inner cluster and that allowed by the tetragonal prismatic nanocapsule mask. This resulted in preferential formation of five bis-adducts (out of 27 possible), two of them bearing a 120° angle between the addends and aligning with the inner TNT cluster trigonal geometry.

title:
Pd(II)-Templated End-to-End
Cyclization of Doubly
N-Confused Bilatrienes: A Stable Singlet Diradicaloid Dye with
Efficient Absorption across the Solar Spectrum
content:
Abstract
We report a highly stable singlet diradicaloid (Pd1-dimer), formed through a Pd(II)-templated end-to-end cyclization of a linear N-confused bilatriene (1). This unique Pd-bridged double-loop complex exhibits an open-shell singlet diradicaloid ground state with an extremely narrow energy gap. Interestingly, further coordination of Pd(II) at the NNCC core generates a distinct doublet radicaloid species (Pd21-dimer). Despite their open-shell electronic nature, both complexes exhibit remarkable stability under ambient conditions and reversible redox interconversion between their corresponding charged states. The complexes display broad visible-to-second near-infrared (NIR-II) absorption profiles arising from extremely narrow energy gaps. Efficient nonradiative relaxation associated with the open-shell electronic structure enables strong photothermal conversion, and Pd1-dimer exhibits a photothermal conversion efficiency of 47.8% in aqueous nanoparticle dispersions under 940 nm laser irradiation. Moreover, when integrated into a carbon nanotube-modified photothermal conversion membrane, applying a small amount of Pd1-dimer (e.g., 1.0 mg per membrane) yields a solar-to-vapor conversion efficiency of 84.4% and an evaporation rate of 1.22 kg m–2 h–1 under 1.0-sun irradiation. This work establishes open-shell porphyrinoid diradicaloids as a promising molecular platform for efficient solar-thermal energy conversion and interfacial seawater desalination.

title:
Layer Engineering of
Quantum Organic–Inorganic
Superlattices by Thermodynamic Design
content:
Abstract
Quantum organic–inorganic superlattices, constructed by vertically stacking two-dimensional inorganic crystals and organic molecular layers, offer a powerful platform for encoding emergent electronic states through an interfacial design. However, the precise layer engineering of such hybrid architectures, particularly the deterministic control over vertical stacking periodicities, has remained elusive because of the absence of a predictive thermodynamic framework governing the staging effect in hybrid systems. Here, we demonstrate that thermodynamic design, based on the quantitative competition between intercalant chemical potential and host elastic deformation energy, provides a principled route to programmable layer engineering of organic–inorganic superlattices. By precisely modulating the chemical potential of the intercalant, we achieve selective access to stage-1 intercalation (alternating 1-layer (1L) molecule/1L-SnSe2) and stage-2 intercalation (alternating 1L-molecule/2L-SnSe2) configurations with high structural fidelity. Atomic-resolution imaging reveals long-range periodic order across both staging phases, while angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the engineered layer sequence directly governs the interfacial charge transfer and electronic band structure evolution. The resulting superlattices exhibit stacking-dependent carrier densities and programmable superconducting transitions, establishing the layer sequence as a synthetic handle for quantum functionality. This work establishes thermodynamic design as a guiding principle for the rational layer engineering of quantum-hybrid solids.

title:
Accelerated
Zeolite Defect Healing Suppresses Oxygen-Containing
Species Trapping for Tandem Propene Epoxidation
content:
Abstract
Selective oxidation of chemical feedstocks with in situ-generated H2O2 offers a sustainable route to high-value oxygenates, yet such tandem catalysis is often fundamentally limited by the trapping of oxygen-containing species, including H2O2-derived intermediates and oxygenated products in zeolite microenvironments, where they undergo nonproductive decomposition and side reactions. Herein, we overcome this limitation by accelerating titanosilicalite hydroxyl defect healing through intensified nucleation and subsequent accelerated crystal growth. The resulting defect-healed microenvironment facilitates the transport of in situ-generated H2O2 between bifunctional active sites while suppressing its nonproductive decomposition to H2O. Moreover, it accelerates product propylene oxide (PO) desorption by weakening hydrogen bond interactions between PO and hydroxyl defects, thereby suppressing ring-opening and overoxidation side reactions. Consequently, the defect-healed Au/TS-1 catalyst exhibits a 1.8-fold enhancement in the PO formation rate and a 2.1-fold increase in Au-based productivity. This defect-healing strategy is broadly applicable to titanosilicates, aluminosilicates, and pure-silica zeolites and can be readily extended to a 10 L scale process, delivering reductions of 21% in production cost and 54% in carbon emissions compared with conventional TS-1 synthesis. Overall, this work establishes a sustainable, scalable, and cost-effective route for zeolite defect healing and provides a general strategy to overcome the long-standing transport-decomposition trade-off in tandem catalysis with in situ-generated H2O2.

title:
Hidden Truchet Architecture
in Zinc  p -Hydroxybenzoate
content:
Abstract
We redetermine the structure of the disordered metal–organic framework Zn(hba) (hba2– = the dianion of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid). Using single-crystal X-ray diffraction measurements, we characterize the structured diffuse scattering that is experimentally observed for this material and which is characteristic of strongly correlated disorder. We use geometric and crystal-chemical arguments to propose a general model for correlated disorder in Zn(hba), and then relate this model to a specific realization of so-called Truchet tilings. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we proceed to show that the model so developed is simultaneously consistent with both the average crystal structure solution described previously and the structured diffuse scattering reported here. The existence of ordered analogues with different but related chemistry suggests scope for control over correlated disorder in this family of metal–organic frameworks. Our study illustrates the potential for a Truchet-tile formalism to help describe and understand more generally the correlated disorder that can occur in network structures.

title:
Chirality-Directed
Molecular Weaving
content:
Abstract
Weaving molecular strands in a manner akin to macroscale fabrics is considered a highly promising strategy for the development of novel polymeric materials. However, existing molecular weaving strategies rely on metal templates or solvent assistance for topological control, which limits molecular weaving to specific conditions. Here, we present a new molecular weaving strategy based on chirality-directed assembly. It can be used in the construction of two-dimensional molecularly woven polymers in various solvents and at different temperatures, all without the use of metal templates or solvent assistance. Furthermore, leveraging the characteristic undulating structure of the woven topology, this strategy provides a unique pathway for tuning the porous separation performance and mechanical properties of molecularly woven materials. These advancements will expedite molecular weaving technology with unprecedented properties.

title:
Isolation of a Silver(0)
Dimer with a Direct Ag–Ag
Bond
content:
Abstract
Despite decades of efforts, molecule featuring a direct Ag(0)–Ag(0) bond has never been isolated─a fundamental challenge that stands in contrast to the established chemistry of gold. Here we report the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of the first molecular Ag(0)–Ag(0) bonded complex, which was stabilized by a tridentate P–Mg–P pincer ligand. Computational studies indicate that the Ag(0)–Ag(0) σ-bond acts as a two-electron donor to the Mg centers. This Ag(0)2 complex reacts with a range of substrates─including selenium, diphenyl diselenide, azobenzene, phenylacetylene, and an isocyanide─to afford a series of heterometallic Mg/Ag products through two-electron reduction processes. These transformations highlight the reducing character of the Ag(0)2 unit and help fill a gap in the periodic trend of coinage-metal chemistry.

title:
A High-Nickel
Cathode Material for Lithium-Ion Batteries
Integrating a Proposed 3D Ionic Percolation Network and Interwoven
Layered/Rock-Salt Nanodomains
content:
Abstract
High-nickel single-crystal cathodes effectively address the poor mechanical stability and severe side reactions that plague their polycrystalline counterparts. However, they introduce new structural challenges, including extended Li+ diffusion pathways, which in turn lead to structural slips, lattice distortions, and phase transformations, ultimately compromising both electrochemical capacity and structural stability. Herein, we report a state-of-the-art cathode architecture for high-nickel materials, derived from high-energy neutron irradiation of single-crystal LiNi0.92Co0.06Mn0.02O2 particles. This process induces long-range Li/Ni antisite disorder and short-range metal–oxygen octahedral distortions, concurrently yielding a nanostructure of abundant grain boundaries and interwoven layered/rock-salt nanodomains within the single-crystalline particles. These grain boundaries are proposed to constitute a 3D percolation network for rapid Li+ transport, whereas the interwoven nanodomains may act as local structural reinforcing units that help suppress irreversible phase transitions and the propagation of interfacial side reactions during cycling. These characteristics are favorable for sustaining continuous Li+ deintercalation/intercalation and reversible electrochemistry, thereby preserving the structural stability of the single-crystal framework while simultaneously shortening diffusion pathways. As a result, the engineered cathode delivers a high specific discharge capacity of 213.9 mAh/g at 0.2 C and 152.2 mAh/g at 10 C (within 4.5 V). Moreover, it retains 80.0% of its initial capacity after 450 cycles at 5 C, significantly outperforming the reference single-crystal cathode (64.2%). This work establishes high-energy neutron irradiation as an effective cathode reconstruction strategy, offering a viable route toward robust, high-energy cathodes.

title:
Enantioselective Coupling
of Unactivated Alkenes with
α-Imino Esters via Alkylzirconium Radical Intermediates
content:
Abstract
Converting simple hydrocarbon feedstocks into stereochemically complex molecules remains a central goal of synthetic chemistry. α-Tetrasubstituted amino acids, which feature densely substituted stereogenic centers and important applications in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, are particularly challenging to access through direct catalytic methods. Here, we report a photoinduced nickel-catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of α-imino esters using alkylzirconium intermediates generated directly from unactivated alkenes. By merging hydrozirconation chemistry with asymmetric radical coupling, the method enables precise control over transient alkyl radicals and their stereoselective incorporation into imine electrophiles. The transformation provides rapid access to diverse α-tetrasubstituted amino acid derivatives from abundant alkene feedstocks, including challenging internal, cyclic, and gaseous alkenes, while accommodating minimally differentiated alkyl substituents. In addition, a copper-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of alkylzirconium reagents with isatin imines was developed. Together, these transformations establish alkene-derived alkylzirconium chemistry as a versatile platform for the asymmetric synthesis of structurally diverse, enantioenriched nitrogen-containing compounds from simple hydrocarbon feedstocks.

title:
A Negative Temperature
Effect on the Reversible Conversion
between Redox Tautomers of Co III (OH) and Co IV (O) Complexes Bearing a Redox-Non-Innocent Tetraamido Macrocyclic
Ligand
content:
Abstract
Elucidating highly reactive intermediates in catalytic reactions relies heavily on cryogenic trapping techniques, where intermediates observed in solution are generally assumed to remain unchanged upon flash-freezing at 77 K. Herein, we demonstrate a striking exception to this long-standing assumption. A cobalt(III)-hydroxo complex bearing a tetraamido macrocyclic ligand radical cation (1: [(TAML•+)CoIII(OH)]−), which is readily observed in solution, is rapidly and quantitatively converted upon freezing to the corresponding cobalt(IV)-oxo complex containing a protonated TAML ligand (2: [(H-TAML)CoIV(O)(HOTf)]−) in the presence of HOTf in acetone. Remarkably, the conversion of 1 to 2 exhibits a negative temperature effect, becoming significantly faster at lower temperatures. Eyring analysis afforded activation parameters of ΔH‡ = −6.0(5) kcal mol–1 and ΔS‡ = −96(7) cal K–1 mol–1. Mechanistic studies reveal that this interconversion proceeds through an acid-assisted proton-coupled electron-transfer (PCET) pathway in which HOTf binding to the redox noninnocent TAML•+ ligand promotes intramolecular electron transfer from the CoIII center to the TAML•+ ligand, coupled with proton transfer from the hydroxo ligand to the TAML framework to produce 2. While the equilibrium constant for the exothermic binding of HOTf increases at lower temperatures, the intrinsic rate constant of the subsequent intramolecular PCET step decreases. Consequently, the overall conversion becomes faster upon cooling because of the interplay between these two processes. This study provides the first example of a negative temperature effect on the reversible conversion between two redox tautomers, demonstrating that cryogenic cooling can drive, rather than simply trap, the interconversion of transient intermediates.

title:
Cu–N 3  Single-Atom Catalysts Enable
High-Turnover C–N and C–O Cross-Coupling of Aryl Electrophiles
content:
Abstract
Transition-metal-catalyzed C–N cross-coupling is fundamental to the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. However, many copper-based catalytic systems rely on exogenous molecular ligands to establish and tune the coordination environment around copper centers, which can increase catalyst-design complexity and complicate catalyst recovery and reuse. We report a copper single-atom catalyst (Cu–N3/OMC) that enables ligand-free C–N and C–O cross-coupling of aryl electrophiles, with isolated Cu sites embedded in a nitrogen-doped carbon framework that provides an intrinsic coordination environment. This system enables ligand-free copper-catalyzed C–N coupling of synthetically relevant aryl bromides and further extends the reaction to less-activated aryl chlorides. A broad range of substituted aryl and heteroaryl bromides─including electron-rich, electron-deficient, ortho-substituted, and fused substrates─undergo efficient coupling with diverse amines and alcohols, affording the corresponding products in moderate to excellent yields (up to 96%). Selected aryl chlorides are also compatible under KI-promoted conditions, albeit with reduced efficiency in some cases. The methodology is applicable to late-stage functionalization of complex pharmaceutical molecules and can be conducted on a preparative scale (5–100 mmol), affording yields of 90–95% and TONs of up to 84,000 under air. TON values were calculated based on the total Cu loading. More broadly, this work suggests that support-engineered coordination environments can influence the reactivity of isolated Cu sites, providing a strategy for ligand-free heteroatom cross-coupling.
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society ASAP

title:
ZnO-Enhanced Cu/ZrO 2  for Photothermal Catalytic
CO 2  Hydrogenation to Methanol
content:
Abstract
The photothermal conversion of CO2 to methanol represents a sustainable pathway for energy storage and carbon neutrality. However, most highly active photothermal catalysts have been evaluated under Xenon-lamp irradiation, in which the photothermal effect arises predominantly from the infrared region. This practice may therefore lead to an underutilization of the ultraviolet (UV) spectrum available in natural solar light. To address this limitation, we designed a composite catalyst by strategically incorporating the semiconductor ZnO into a Cu/ZrO2 system. This design enables complementary light absorption: Cu effectively harnesses visible/near-infrared light, while ZnO extends the response into the UV range. Comprehensive characterizations confirm that the introduction of Zn significantly enhances the light-harvesting capability without altering the Cu active sites. Consequently, the optimized Cu/ZrO2–ZnO catalyst exhibits a remarkable enhancement in photothermal reaction, particularly under UV light, while maintaining CO2 hydrogenation activity. When evaluated under concentrated real sunlight, the catalyst achieves a methanol production rate of 2.7 mmol g–1 h–1, attributable to its efficient full-spectrum utilization. This work not only provides an efficient catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation but also demonstrates a general strategy for maximizing solar energy conversion in photothermal catalysis.

title:
Dual-Functional Structure-Directing
Agents Enable
High-Loading Encapsulation of Ultrasmall Metal Nanoparticles in Zeolites
content:
Abstract
Confined ultrasmall metal nanoparticles within zeolite crystals have emerged as promising catalysts due to their exceptional thermal stability and high catalytic activity under harsh reaction conditions. However, their loading amounts are limited to 1.0 mol % relative to SiO2, mainly due to steric hindrance and competition between metal species and structure-directing agents (SDAs) for access to micropores. Here, we introduce a molecular design strategy that unifies metal coordination and zeolite templating within a single dual-functional SDA molecule. This approach enables elevated metal loadings (up to ∼2.4 mol % relative to SiO2) of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. This strategy is applicable to multiple microporous frameworks, including MFI zeolites and AFI aluminophosphate, allowing encapsulation of Cu, Co, and Pt nanoparticles. The metal encapsulation by microporous crystals renders them stable under harsh reaction conditions (e.g., high temperature) and thereby suppresses catalyst deactivation through sintering during the methane dry reforming reaction. We believe that our approach offers a molecular design principle for the synthesis of high-loading, sintering-resistant, zeolite-encapsulated catalysts.

title:
Stable Open-Shell Bowl-Shaped
Cycloarene with Multiple
Hybrid Spin–Spin Coupling and Tunable Radical Characters
content:
Abstract
The precise syntheses of well-defined cycloarenes and stable open-shell polyradicaloids are two challenging topics in chemistry and materials science. Herein, the first example of a cycloarene polyradicaloid molecule (CPR) with three types of adjacent spin–spin coupling was successfully synthesized in single-crystal form by fusing Chichibabin, Schlenk, and o-quinodimethane hydrocarbons into a conjugated double-stranded bowl structure. It exhibits a small singlet–triplet energy gap, significant polyradical characters, and remarkable stability (t1/2 = 110 days in air-saturated solution). Interestingly, CPR adapts a rigid oval-bowl-shaped configuration and demonstrates fascinating encapsulation of fullerenes C60 and C70. Crucially, various experimental results confirm that the intramolecular spin–spin interactions can be effectively modulated by an electron-accepting guest, which represents the first systematic study of the radical characters in π-conjugated polyradicaloids by a supramolecular assembly strategy. Our findings provide a new approach for constructing stable cycloarene polyradicaloids and a novel strategy for manipulating radical spin coupling.

title:
Regenerable Heterogeneous
Palladium Single-Atom Catalysts
for Direct C–H Arylation
content:
Abstract
Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer tunable, recoverable heterogeneous alternatives to homogeneous metal complexes in handle-based cross-coupling reactions. However, their application to direct C–H bond functionalization remains unexplored beyond photochemical methods, as the elevated temperature and demanding reaction conditions place stringent requirements on catalyst stability. Here, we demonstrate a Pd single-atom-catalyzed C–H arylation of indoles, extending heterogeneous SACs to thermal C–H functionalization and achieving cumulative turnover numbers above 200 across five cycles. Among diverse oxygen- and nitrogen-coordinated SACs, nitrogen-coordinated sites in Pd@C3N4 uniquely combined metal retention with high activity after phosphine activation. Recycling studies coupled with in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal Pd–I bond formation as the dominant catalyst deactivation pathway. Guided by this insight, postreaction treatment in aqueous ammonia overcomes iodide poisoning, enabling catalytic activity over multiple cycles. These findings establish design principles for balancing activity, stability, and regenerability in Pd SACs for demanding C–H functionalizations, advancing their potential for greener, more step-efficient chemical synthesis.

title:
Surface-Layer Pore
Aperture Engineering in a Metal–Organic
Framework for High-Capacity CO 2 /C 2 H 2  Molecular Sieving
content:
Abstract
Molecular sieving in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is commonly achieved by narrowing the entire pore network, which enhances size exclusion but often sacrifices adsorption capacity. Here we report surface-layer pore aperture engineering as a spatially decoupled strategy for high-capacity CO2/C2H2 molecular sieving. Through surface-confined coordination modification of a copper-based MOF, the external pore apertures were selectively regulated while the internal adsorption space was largely preserved. Microscopy, elemental mapping, depth-resolved XPS, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support the formation of a surface-confined functional shell at the pore aperture. The modified framework converts a nonselective, high-capacity adsorbent into a CO2/C2H2 molecular sieve. BUT-169-NH2-TRZ retains a high CO2 uptake of 90.3 cm3 g–1 at 298 K and 1 bar while suppressing C2H2 adsorption to 2.7 cm3 g–1, representing a new benchmark for CO2/C2H2 sieving separation. Further optimization with hexylamine affords faster CO2 transport and dynamic CO2/C2H2 separation, delivering a high productivity of 1.13 mol kg–1 for C2H2 (purity > 99.99%) over repeated breakthrough cycles. This work establishes surface-layer pore aperture engineering as a route to overcome the conventional selectivity–capacity trade-off in molecular sieving separations.

title:
Redox Buffering and
Corrosion in Molten Chloride Salts
Dictated by Chlorobasicity
content:
Abstract
This study establishes an in situ synchrotron approach to directly link molten-salt chemistry, redox-buffer speciation, and alloy corrosion in chloride melts. Using a first-of-its-kind corrosion cell coupled to simultaneous X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray fluorescence (XRF), we monitor europium redox-buffer speciation and chromium dissolution during corrosion of Ni-20Cr in molten LiCl-KCl and KCl-MgCl2 salts. To build a mechanistic framework, we combine UV–vis optical basicity measurements, in situ electrochemistry, and molecular dynamics simulations to quantify how salt chlorobasicity reshapes europium solvation and shifts the Eu(III)/Eu(II) apparent potential. Increasing MgCl2 content drives the apparent potential of the Eu(III)/Eu(II) couple +0.49 V relative to LiCl-KCl and stabilizes Eu(II)-compatible solvation environments. In situ, time-resolved Eu L3-edge XANES reveals progressive Eu(III) reduction in KCl-MgCl2 melts, while Eu(III) remains predominantly stable in LiCl-KCl. This behavior is consistent with a chlorobasicity-activated reaction with boron nitride (BN) cell components. In less chlorobasic melts, salt redox chemistry enables BN chlorination, allowing BN to act as a sacrificial reductant and chlorinating agent that promotes Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion, whereas this pathway is not thermodynamically favored in LiCl-KCl. During active corrosion of Ni-20Cr, coupled Eu XANES and Cr XRF measurements show concurrent Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion and Cr dissolution, confirming that Eu(III) is the oxidizing species driving chromium oxidation. Together, these results demonstrate that chlorobasicity is a central control variable for redox-buffer speciation and corrosion thermodynamics, and more broadly that chlorobasicity can enable or suppress reactive pathways with structural materials in high-temperature molten salts.

title:
Constructing Dinuclear
Cd 2 -Porphyrin
Motifs in Metal–Organic Frameworks to Accelerate Intersystem
Crossing for Boosting Photocatalytic Aerobic Oxidation
content:
Abstract
Dinuclear metalloporphyrin cores remain elusive in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), despite their potential to direct spin–orbit coupling and triplet sensitization for efficient singlet oxygen (1O2) generation. Herein, we report a structurally precise series of Cd-porphyrin MOFs to elucidate how porphyrin-core nuclearity and coordination geometry influence 1O2 photosensitization. Solvothermal regulation affords three crystalline porous frameworks featuring a free-base porphyrin core (QPF-8), a mononuclear Cd-porphyrin unit (QPF-9), and a dinuclear Cd2-porphyrin motif (QPF-10). QPF-8 serves as an additional free-base reference, whereas the closely related QPF-9 and QPF-10 provide a direct platform for probing how mono- and dinuclear porphyrin coordination environments influence photophysical properties. QPF-10 exhibits a measured 1O2 quantum yield of 0.68, compared with 0.50 for QPF-9. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations associate the dinuclear motif with enhanced metal-porphyrin orbital mixing and a 4.59-fold increase in the calculated S1–T1 spin–orbit coupling matrix element (from 3.14 to 14.40 cm–1), supporting more effective triplet photosensitization. Consistent with these photophysical properties, QPF-10 demonstrates superior catalytic activity in the aerobic photooxidation of 1,5-dihydroxynaphthalene. Notably, its activity is approximately twice that of the archetypal PCN-224(Zn) and also exceeds that of the Pt-based QPF-1(Pt). These results identify dinuclear porphyrin coordination as a structural strategy for enhancing triplet photosensitization in crystalline heterogeneous catalysts.
